findings.text: Mmap staging object keeps a reference to the virtual mapping plus a filename pointer with its padded length plus device major and minor plus inode number and generation plus derived protection and mapping flags plus a build identifier buffer with its valid length plus an embedded output record holding a header and process and thread identifiers and mapping start and length and file offset. The embedded record is the fixed prefix emitted before extended identity and name bytes.

Per subscriber filtering for mapping notifications depends on mapping executability and subscriber wishes: non executable mappings require data interest while executable mappings require mapping interest in either basic or extended form. Output chooses basic or extended record type from subscriber extended interest, enlarges the payload for identity and attribute fields when extended, marks user origin and optionally build identifier presence and data origin, initializes header with computed size, aborts quietly when output reservation fails, fills process and thread ids for current task, emits fixed prefix then either build identifier size prefix plus buffer or device and inode identity followed by protection and flags, then filename bytes, then identifier sample trailer.

Mapping notification entry skips all work when no mapping subscribers are counted, otherwise seeds start length and offset from mapping bounds and page offset, refreshes address filters, then builds the report. Protection derives from read write execute mapping properties, sharing derives from may share property with locked and hugetlb additions, file backed mappings resolve a printable path with distinct sentinels for allocation failure and overlong path and capture device and inode identity from the file inode, non file mappings prefer operation provided name then architecture name then heap stack or anonymous sentinels, short names are copied to a small temporary and padded with zeros to a multiple of eight bytes, build identifier parsing occurs only when build identifier subscribers are counted, broadcast iterates over subscriber set, temporary path storage is released.

Address filter relevance needs a filter path present and equality between filter dentry inode and mapping file inode plus overlap between filter offset interval and mapping offset interval. Clipping sets the result range to the intersection of the two intervals expressed in virtual addresses, handling filter starting before mapping versus inside mapping. Per event adjustment walks the filter list and stores one clipped range per filter, counts successful clips, bumps a generation counter only when at least one clip succeeded, and requests an event stop after releasing the lock in that case. Top level adjustment ignores non executable mappings and mappings without files and operates on the current task context obtained under read side protection only when context exists and only for subscribers that actually use filters.

Public notifications provided are mapping setup for a virtual mapping, auxiliary trace chunk announcement with head offset size and flags, and lost sample count announcement. The auxiliary and lost forms build a small fixed record with header plus payload, initialize header with their record type and zero misc and full size, abort on reservation failure, emit fixed part then identifier sample trailer then close output.

Context switch staging holds task and next or previous task references plus an embedded record with header and next or previous process and thread identifiers plus flags for sched in versus out and preemption. Task scoped subscribers receive a short header only record of one type while system wide subscribers receive the full record with identifiers of another type, misc encodes out versus in plus a preemption addition, header initialization and reservation failure handling and trailer emission follow the common output pattern with per subscriber gating on context switch interest.

Kernel symbol staging holds a name pointer with padded length plus embedded record with header and address and length and symbol type and flags. Per subscriber gating uses ksymbol interest, output size is fixed prefix plus name length, payload order is fixed prefix then name bytes then trailer. Entry skips when no ksymbol subscribers, rejects unknown or out of range types with a one time warning, copies the name into a bounded buffer and pads with zeros to eight byte multiple, sets an unregister flag from the boolean, seeds address length type and flags, then broadcasts.

BPF staging holds a program reference plus embedded record with header and event type and flags and identifier and tag bytes. Per subscriber gating uses BPF interest, output is fixed size with trailer. Load and unload first emit kernel symbol notifications for the main program address and length and name and for each auxiliary function beyond the first when ksymbol subscribers exist, with unload selecting unregister semantics. Other BPF types return without action, and BPF broadcast is skipped when no BPF subscribers exist. The tag is copied verbatim and its size is asserted to be a multiple of eight.

Deferred callchain staging holds an unwind trace reference plus an embedded record with header and cookie and entry count followed by variable address entries. Output size is fixed prefix plus eight bytes per trace entry, gating uses deferred output interest with user misc, payload order is fixed prefix then each trace entry in order then trailer. The unwind completion callback builds this staging from supplied trace and cookie and broadcasts to all subscribers.

Text poke staging holds old and new byte pointers plus total variable length and padding and both lengths plus embedded record with header and target address. Total accounts for both length prefixes plus both payloads rounded up to eight byte multiple with explicit zero padding. Per subscriber gating uses text poke interest with kernel misc, payload order is fixed prefix then old length then new length then old bytes then new bytes then zero padding then trailer. Entry skips when no text poke subscribers and otherwise computes total and padding and broadcasts.

Instruction trace start marking sets an attach state flag on the given event by read modify write. Auxiliary hardware identity reporting redirects a child event to its parent when a parent exists, then emits a fixed record carrying the supplied hardware identifier with its dedicated type and trailer.

Interrupt accounting compares a per CPU throttle sequence with the event stored sequence to reset or increment a per event interrupt count, and when throttling is requested and the count reaches a global per tick limit it increments a per CPU throttled count, marks the CPU as needing tick handling for perf, throttles the event group, and reports throttled. Frequency mode captures current time, updates the stored timestamp, and adjusts the sampling period from the elapsed delta and last period only for positive deltas below twice the tick interval. Sampling permission denies kernel register state when the subscriber excludes kernel, otherwise allows.

Overflow delivery to BPF has two compiled variants. The active variant builds a kernel view coupling sample data and event, resolves user register view, guards reentrancy with a per CPU active counter that must be one to proceed, loads the attached program under read side protection, prepares the sample, runs the program, then decrements the counter and returns the program result. The fallback variant always reports handled without action. Program release in the active variant clears the event program reference and drops a reference when present, while the fallback variant does nothing.

Address filter range refresh holds the filter head raw spinlock with interrupt state saved across the list walk and range stores and conditional generation increment, releasing before any stop request. Current task context lookup for that refresh is enclosed in read side critical section. BPF program load during overflow handling is enclosed in read side critical section with single read semantics.

Iteration callbacks invoked by subscriber walks are mapping output, address filter adjustment, switch output, ksymbol output, BPF output, deferred callchain output, and text poke output, plus the unwind completion callback that fans out deferred records. Each receives an event plus opaque staging and decides internally whether the event opted into that record kind before emitting.

Path buffer allocation uses a large fixed size and falls back to sentinel names rather than failing, overlong paths use a distinct sentinel, non file mappings never dereference absent operations, filename and symbol name tails are zero filled to eight byte boundary to avoid exposing uninitialized bytes, ksymbol type misuse triggers a one time warning instead of emitting, output reservation failures silently skip one record, text poke lengths come from the caller and determine copy amounts and padding.

User visible record identities include mapping basic and extended, auxiliary data, lost samples, switch short and cpu wide, kernel symbol, BPF event, deferred callchain, text poke, and auxiliary hardware identity. Misc attributes distinguish user versus kernel origin and data mapping versus executable mapping and build identifier presence and switch out versus in and preemption. Symbol handling uses a maximum type bound plus unknown and BPF type values plus an unregister flag. Memory attribute mapping uses read write execute to protection bits and shared versus private plus locked and hugetlb to mapping flags. BPF load versus unload select register versus unregister symbol semantics.

Throttle counting moves between reset on observed sequence change and increment on same sequence, with a transition to throttled group state and tick dependency marked when the per tick limit is reached. Address filter generation stays unchanged when no range clips and increments once per mapping update when at least one filter clips, followed by a stop request. Instruction trace attachment is monotonic flag set once started. BPF symbol visibility toggles between registered on load and unregistered on unload.
